shared_elements: low-relief carving on a vertical stone surface
upper register of repeated small motifs across the top
curved/arc or disc-like form near the top
figures (animal in A, human-like in B) shown in profile within the upper scene
lower field treated as a large, distinct panel
justification: Both are vertical stone slabs organised into a busy upper figural register capped by repeated motifs and an arc/disc form, cut off by a horizontal band above a large lower panel, which gives a genuinely comparable compositional skeleton. The rendering differs sharply, however: A uses bold, flat, schematic silhouettes of animals with heavy outlines, while B shows finely modelled small-scale figures over a dense field of incised linear script, so the manner of carving looks nothing alike.
